library(jsonlite)

## API Key Setup (.Renviron)

```{r renviron-setup, eval=FALSE}
# Run once to open your user .Renviron file:
usethis::edit_r_environ()

# Add this line in the file, then save:
# NASA_API_KEY=your_key_here

# Restart R, then verify:
Sys.getenv("NASA_API_KEY")
```

## Part A: No-Auth API (Open-Meteo)

```{r open-meteo-call}
# Build the request URL for Washington, DC
lat <- 38.9072
lon <- -77.0369

meteo_url <- paste0(
  "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?",
  "latitude=", lat,
  "&longitude=", lon,
  "&daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum",
  "&timezone=auto"
)

meteo_raw <- fromJSON(meteo_url)
weather_df <- as.data.frame(meteo_raw$daily)

weather_df <- weather_df %>%
  select(time, temperature_2m_max, precipitation_sum)

head(weather_df)
```

```{r open-meteo-summary}
weather_summary <- weather_df %>%
  summarize(
    avg_max_temp = mean(temperature_2m_max, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_precip = sum(precipitation_sum, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

weather_summary
```

## Part B: API Key Auth (NASA APOD)

```{r nasa-call}
nasa_key <- Sys.getenv("NASA_API_KEY")
if (nasa_key == "") {
  message("NASA_API_KEY not found; using DEMO_KEY (lower rate limits).")
  nasa_key <- "DEMO_KEY"
}

nasa_url <- paste0(
  "https://api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod?",
  "start_date=2026-03-01",
  "&end_date=2026-03-07",
  "&api_key=", nasa_key
)

nasa_raw <- fromJSON(nasa_url)
apod_df <- as.data.frame(nasa_raw)

apod_df <- apod_df %>%
  select(any_of(c("date", "title", "media_type", "url")))

head(apod_df)
```

```{r nasa-summary}
apod_counts <- apod_df %>%
  count(media_type, sort = TRUE)

apod_counts
```

## Reflection

1. What changed in your workflow between no-auth and key-auth APIs?
2. Which API was easier to clean and why?
3. What reliability risk did you encounter or anticipate?
